text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A states a clear position upfront ('I personaly would never use one of these cars') and maintains it throughout, ending with a consistent conclusion.", "quality": "Clear sustained position", "description": "The essay states and maintains a single coherent argumentative stance from introduction to conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Essay A references specific article details like the vibrating seat, flashing lights, and the car watching the driver.", "quality": "Relevant evidence use", "description": "The essay draws on concrete details from the source article to support its argument rather than drifting off-topic."}, {"evidence": "Essay A has a recognizable structure with an opening position, body paragraphs developing reasons, and a concluding restatement of the argument.", "quality": "Organized structure", "description": "The essay follows a logical introduction-body-conclusion progression that keeps the argument focused."}, {"evidence": "Essay A develops reasons such as risk of malfunction, safety concerns, and privacy objections, each tied back to the central claim.", "quality": "Reasoned argument development", "description": "The essay builds multiple supporting reasons that connect to the overall position rather than listing disconnected points."}, {"evidence": "Essay B wanders across unrelated topics such as texting while driving, kids driving ages, and presidential policy changes, losing focus on the driverless car question.", "quality": "Focused argumentation", "description": "The essay stays on the assigned topic of driverless cars rather than digressing into tangential complaints about drivers and laws."}]}
